name: list_spaces
description: List the spaces of the knowledge base and boards the user can read: their private space and the shared spaces they belong to, with whether they may write each.

name: list_members
description: List the people who can be assigned a card: the members of the workspace, or, with space_id, the people who have access to that space (a shared space's members, or a private space's owner). Returns each person's id, name and email, and their role. create_card and update_card take the id as assignee.id; use space_id with the card's space, since the assignee must be able to see it. Only what the user can read is listed. People come by id; when the reply has next_cursor there are more: call again with it as cursor.

space_id.description: the space, from list_spaces; leave it out for the whole workspace's members

cursor.description: the next_cursor of the previous reply, for the people after it; leave it out for the first page

name: search_docs
description: Search the knowledge base: every space the user can read, or one space. Returns paths, titles and the passages that matched; read a document with read_doc.

name: list_docs
description: List the documents and files of a space, by path, a page at a time: pass the reply's "next" as "after" for the next page. Each has its size and "versioned": false for large files and audio and video, of which only the current version is kept.

folder.description: only what is in this folder

name: read_doc
description: Read a Markdown document (.md). Long documents come in pieces of 32 KiB: pass "next_offset" as "offset" for the next piece. "version" is what write_doc needs to change it.

name: write_doc
description: Create or replace a Markdown document (.md) in a space the user may write. To create one, leave out base_version; to replace one, pass the version you read. The change is the user's, made by their agent, and kept in the history.

base_version.description: the version from read_doc, to replace a document

name: list_boards
description: List a space's boards: its personal board, or its team boards.

name: list_cards
description: List a board's cards in board order (bodies shortened). Filter by column, assignee ("user" with assignee_id, "agent" or "none"), blocked, labels, due dates, overdue, or text in the title or body; sort by due date. Each card shows its due date (YYYY-MM-DD or null) and labels.

labels.description: only cards that have all of these labels (normalized like card labels)

due_before.description: only cards due on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD

due_after.description: only cards due on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD

overdue.description: true: only cards due before today that aren't done or archived

today.description: the user's date today, for overdue; default today in UTC

sort.description: board (default): by column, then position; due: soonest due date first, cards without one last

name: show_card
description: Show a card with its whole body and its comment thread (the newest comments, if there are many).

name: create_card
description: Add a card to a board. Only the title is required; it goes last in the backlog unless told otherwise.

id.description: the user, for kind "user", from list_members

assignee.description: who the card is for: a member who can see the space, or the agent; null for nobody

blocked_by.description: cards of the same board this one waits for

docs.description: paths of documents in the same space

conversations.description: conversation IDs; only the user's own conversations can be added

due.description: the due date, a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD with no time; null for none

labels.description: free-text labels, kept case folded (as 'bug' for 'Bug'); a short list of what the card is about

name: update_card
description: Change a card: only the fields given change; lists (blocked_by, docs, conversations, labels) replace the whole list, null clears a field (due too).

version.description: the version of the card you last read; if it changed since, the call fails: read it again first

id.description: the user, for kind "user", from list_members

assignee.description: who the card is for: a member who can see the space, or the agent; null for nobody

blocked_by.description: cards of the same board this one waits for

docs.description: paths of documents in the same space

conversations.description: conversation IDs; only the user's own conversations can be added

due.description: the due date, a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD with no time; null for none

labels.description: free-text labels, kept case folded (as 'bug' for 'Bug'); replaces all the card's labels; [] clears them

name: move_card
description: Move a card to a column, at a 0-based position (last if left out).

version.description: the version of the card you last read; if it changed since, the call fails: read it again first

name: comment_card
description: Add a comment to a card's thread.

name: set_blocked
description: Say why a card is blocked and which cards of the board it waits for; reason null and no cards unblock it.

version.description: the version of the card you last read; if it changed since, the call fails: read it again first

name: app_catalog
description: What a personal app may be made of: the components and their props, the functions, the collection's field types, the actions, the rules, and an example app. Read it before create_app or update_app.

name: list_apps
description: List a space's personal apps (without their definitions); archived: true includes the ones taken offline. A list too long for one reply is cut short, with truncated: true and next_offset: call again with that offset for the rest.

offset.description: apps to skip, from a previous reply's next_offset; 0 by default

name: show_app
description: Show an app: its DRAFT definition (screen, collection, actions and summaries: what you edit), its version, and which release is live (number, definition_version and what it requires, not its definition) with unpublished_changes, whether the draft differs from it. People use the live release, not the draft.

name: list_app_rows
description: Read an app's data: the rows the user may read (all of them, or only the ones they created, by their role in the app), oldest first, each with its id, its _revision and the fields its collection declares (an attachment field holds a list of {id, content_type, size, width, height}: the agent can read what photos a row has, never their bytes, and can't upload or attach one). Deleted rows are not listed. An offline app's rows are kept and read too. A list too long for one reply is cut short, with truncated: true and next_after: call again with after set to it for the rest.

after.description: only rows after this row id, from a previous reply's next_after: rows added or removed meanwhile don't shift the pages

name: query_app_rows
description: Query an app's data with filters, search, sort and pages, and get totals over ALL the rows that match, not only the page: the rows the user may read (all of them, or only the ones they created, by their role in the app), each with its id, its _revision and the fields its live release's collection declares. Use it instead of list_app_rows when you need some rows, an order, a count or a sum. Filters all have to hold: a field, an op (eq, ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, or contains for a string) and a value of the field's type; a row with no value of the field equals nothing (ne matches it, the others don't). search is words that each have to be in some string or choice field. Rows are ordered by sort (a field, _updated, _created or id; _updated newest first by default) and then by id, rows without a value last; a page ends with next_cursor, which you pass as cursor, with the same query, for the next one: rows added or removed meanwhile don't shift the pages. total and aggregates are over every matching row. A number held as text is shown but is in no comparison, sort or sum. A page too long for one reply is made shorter: next_cursor continues after the last row sent.

state.description: live rows (the default) or deleted ones, which can be restored by a person

field.description: a field the app's live release declares

op.description: lt, lte, gt and gte are for number, date, time and string fields; contains is a case-insensitive substring of a string field

value.description: a value of the field's type: text, a number, true or false, a date YYYY-MM-DD or a time HH:MM

filters.description: conditions that all have to hold

search.description: words (at most 5) that each have to be in some string or choice field, in any case

sort.description: a field, or _updated, _created, _deleted (deleted rows only) or id

dir.description: the times are newest first by default, the rest ascending

cursor.description: the previous page's next_cursor, with the same state, filters, search and sort

field.description: count: optional (the rows that have a value of it); sum and avg: a number field; min and max: a number, date or time field

aggregates.description: values over all the matching rows, each with the count of rows it was computed from

name: create_app
description: Save a new personal app in a space the user may write: a private space's apps are the user's, a shared space's are its members'. The server checks the definition against the catalog and says what is wrong if it doesn't fit. It is saved as a draft: it can't be launched until a person who may publish the app publishes it in the Apps page; you can't publish.

definition.description: what the app is made of: read app_catalog first. The server checks it strictly against the catalog.

definition_version.description: the version of the definition's format; leave it out for the current one, 2. A definition that says 1 can't use screens, time, choice, attachment, location, signature or barcode fields, rules or navigation

requires.description: the catalog capabilities the screen needs: the server works them out and replaces whatever is given

components.description: the screen of an app with ONE screen: A2UI v0.9 components from app_catalog, each {"id", "component", …props}, one with the id "root". An app with several screens has screens instead, never both

screens.description: the screens of an app with several: each {"name", "root", "record"?, "components"}. root is the id of the screen's root component (not "root"); all component ids are unique across the screens, and a component refers only to its own screen's. At most 300 components in all. record: true is a detail screen, opened with a record's id and showing it at /record. Buttons move between screens with a navigate action

entry.description: the screen an app with screens opens on; it can't be a record screen

type.description: a date is YYYY-MM-DD, a time HH:MM on a 24-hour clock, a choice one of its options, an attachment a list of photos (JPEG, PNG or GIF) that people upload with the PhotoInput component: you can't upload or read pictures, only see their ids and metadata in list_app_rows; a location {lat, lon, accuracy_m, captured_at, source} that people capture with the LocationInput component, a signature one PNG that they draw with SignatureInput (both can't be changed once stored, unless the field is editable), a barcode the text of a code they scan or type with BarcodeInput

required_when.description: the field is required when this rule holds of the row, enforced on every insert and update whatever a screen shows: {"field", "op": eq|ne|lt|lte|gt|gte, "value": a literal of that field's type} or {"all": [rules]} or {"any": [rules]}, nested at most 3 deep, at most 16 parts. Not for a field that is always required

options.description: a choice field's options: different texts, at most 100 characters each

option_labels.description: a choice field's labels, as {"<option>": "<label>"} (each key one of the options, each label 1 to 100 characters): how a stored value reads to people. A screen shows a choice's label by binding to _labels/<field> (in a List template) or /record/_labels/<field>, never the field itself, which holds the stored text

max_length.description: string and barcode fields; 1000 if left out

max_files.description: attachment fields: how many photos; 1 if left out

max_bytes.description: attachment and signature fields: the size of each file in bytes; 8 MiB if left out for photos, 1 MiB for a signature

capture.description: location fields: take the position when the person presses the button (default) or when they submit the form; once, in the foreground, never in the background. An event context entry that passes a submit field is named as the field

format.description: barcode fields: the kind of code scanned; any if left out. ean_8, ean_13, upc_a and upc_e are checked as digits (with their check digit, but upc_e's)

editable.description: location and signature fields: let a stored value be changed later; by default it can't be

actions.description: event name → what it does; a Button's event must name one

screen.description: navigate: the screen it opens. The Button's event context is {"id": …} for a record screen, none otherwise

then.description: insert, update or delete: the screen to open once it has run (not a record screen)

effects.description: insert or update only: what the change sets going on boards and documents once the record is saved, done by the server as the user who acted and only if they still may (a card or document is never made twice). Each is one of the registry's kinds with the fields it takes, and nothing else is accepted: no URLs, no tool names. Text fields are templates: {{field}} is a field of the collection, {{id}} the record's number, and there is nothing more to them

kind.description: create_card: a card on a board; update_card: moves the card a create_card effect made for this record; create_document: a Markdown document in a space; open_route: a place in TaskTo.AI to open (route board, card or document)

name.description: create_card only: names the effect so update_card and an open_route card can refer to the card it made. Unique in the app

when.description: the effect applies only if this rule (the same as required_when) holds of the record as the change leaves it

space_id.description: create_card, create_document, open_route board or document: the space, by ID. The person who saves and publishes the app must be able to write it, and whoever acts must be able to when the effect runs

board_id.description: create_card, open_route board: the board of that space, by ID

column.description: create_card: where the card goes (default backlog); update_card: where it moves

title.description: create_card: the card's title, a template of at most 400 characters

body.description: create_card: the card's Markdown body, a template

docs.description: create_card: documents of the board's space the card refers to, templates of paths

card.description: update_card, open_route card: the name of the create_card effect whose card for the record it is about

path.description: create_document, open_route document: a template of a path inside the space, like inspections/{{id}}.md. A create_document path ends in .md, never starts with / and has no ... Whatever fills a hole is made a safe file name

content.description: create_document: the document's text, a template

summaries.description: values computed from the rows, at /<name> in the data model

field.description: the number field a sum adds

where.description: count or sum only the rows this rule holds of (the same rule as required_when)

contributions.description: what the app offers the Home page and the navigation (version 2 of the format): widgets people may put on their Home, and the pin's label. A widget is a bounded view, never markup: it shows summaries, one of the app's screens, or is only a shortcut that opens the app. Nothing here grants access: every widget reads and acts through the app, with the person's own role

id.description: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits or _ (at most 40), unique in the app

title.description: plain text of 1 to 60 characters on one line

summaries.description: summaries widget only: 1 to 4 of the app's summaries, each with its label

summary.description: the name of one of the app's summaries

screen.description: screen widget only: one of the app's screens that doesn't show a record
the screen the pin opens the app on (not a record screen); the entry if left out

name: update_app
description: Change an app: rename it, replace its DRAFT definition, or take it offline (archived: true; its rows are kept) and back. Only what is given changes. A new definition changes nothing people use: they keep the live release until a person who may publish the app publishes the draft, which checks it against the app's rows (add new fields as optional, and keep the names and types of fields that have data, or the publisher has to acknowledge the change); you can't publish or roll back. The user's role in the app decides: renaming and redefining need the right to design it, taking it offline the right to publish it; without it the call is refused (403), and only the user's own roles count, not anything in the definition.

version.description: the version of the app you last read; if it changed since, the call fails: read it again first

name: browser_tabs
description: List the open tabs of the user's browser: id, title, URL, and whether you opened it. Doesn't start the browser.

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_open
description: Open a URL in a new tab of the user's browser, starting it if it isn't running. Returns the tab; then read the page with browser_snapshot. Use the personal browser for the user's own accounts (it keeps their logins) and the testing one to try apps with nothing of the user's in it.

url.description: an http or https address, or about:blank

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_navigate
description: Load a URL in a tab.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

url.description: an http or https address, or about:blank

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_snapshot
description: Read a tab's page as text: its title, URL and visible text, with each link, button and field on a line that starts with its ref, such as [e12] button "Sign in". Use the refs with browser_click and browser_type, and take a new snapshot after the page changes. Password values are never shown, and frames (such as captchas) are named but not read.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_click
description: Click an element of a tab, by its ref from the last snapshot, with a real mouse click. Returns the tab as it is after the click.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

ref.description: the element's ref from the last browser_snapshot of the tab, such as e12

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_type
description: Type text into a field of a tab, by its ref from the last snapshot, replacing what is in it; with submit, press Enter after. Never type a password, a 2FA code or anything secret: ask the user to do it with browser_help.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

ref.description: the element's ref from the last browser_snapshot of the tab, such as e12

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_press
description: Press a key in a tab: Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Delete, Space, the arrows, PageUp, PageDown, Home or End.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_close
description: Close a tab you opened. The user's own tabs can't be closed.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

browser.description: personal (the default): the user's own browser, with their logins, which they can watch and take over; testing: a clean headless browser with no profile, emptied each time it starts, for trying apps

name: browser_help
description: Ask the user to take over the personal browser when a site needs them: to sign in, solve a captcha, enter a 2FA code or anything secret, or decide something. The tab is brought to the front, and the user sees a card with your message and a live view of the browser. Then end your turn at once, saying in one short sentence what they need to do. They will tell you when they are done (or that they won't do it now); take a new snapshot before you go on.

tab.description: the tab's id, from browser_tabs or browser_open

message.description: what the user should do, in a sentence or two
